 Slovenia vs Switzerland Preview & Prediction | 2026-27 UEFA Nations League | League B
 by Alex Sarwar · 11 November 2026 at 9:01 am 
 Post 
 Share 
 Click here for today’s sports betting tips from our expert analysts! 
 Victory over Slovenia would leave Switzerland one win away from a flawless group stage campaign which has seen them already secure promotion to League A. 
 Kick-off date/time: 
 13 November 2026 at 7:45 pm 
 How to watch on TV:  UK – Amazon Prime Video / USA – FOX Sports
 How to watch online:  UK – Amazon Prime Video / USA – FOX Sports streaming platforms
 Key stats 
 Switzerland won the only previous Nations League meeting between the sides, 2-1 in Lucerne on Matchday 3 of this edition.
 Coming into Matchday 5, Switzerland top Group B1 with a 100% record – 12 points from four matches – and are five points clear of second-placed Slovenia.
 Switzerland's four consecutive wins are their longest winning run in 28 Nations League matches.
 Switzerland have scored 11 goals and conceded only once in this edition, and are one of three teams with a 100% record after four matches, along with Portugal and Spain.
 Switzerland's revival follows a 2024/25 campaign in which they finished bottom of Group A4 with two points and no wins from six matches.
 Switzerland have scored in each of their last seven Nations League matches.
 Switzerland have won only four of their 14 away Nations League matches (D1 L9), although two of those wins have come in this edition, both 3-0, against North Macedonia and Scotland.
 Slovenia have kept clean sheets in each of their last three home Nations League matches, including a 0-0 draw with Scotland and a 2-0 win over North Macedonia in this edition.
 Slovenia have lost only three of their 15 home Nations League matches (W6 D6).
 Slovenia have won two of their four Nations League matches on Matchday 5 (D1 L1), while Switzerland are unbeaten in three on Matchday 5 (W1 D2).
 Benjamin Sesko has scored eight goals in 14 Nations League appearances, twice as many as any other Slovenia player.
 Haris Seferovic has scored seven goals in 17 Nations League appearances, the most of any Switzerland player.
 Will Switzerland finish with a perfect 18 points from 18 in Group B1?
 Open poll and results 
 Slovenia vs Switzerland prediction 
 Switzerland have been nigh on perfect so far in Group B1. They've won four out of four and scored a whopping 11 goals along the way. Murat Yakin's side have combined cutting-edge attacking play with an excellent defence that, as it stands, has conceded just once.
However, it was Slovenia who gave the Swiss their toughest challenge during the previous international break, narrowly losing 2-1 in Lucerne. Switzerland fell behind in that game before rallying quickly to go in front before half-time, before holding that lead throughout the second half.
Another tough assignment is likely here, as Slovenia will try to make the most of having home advantage. Even so, Switzerland are by far the best team in this group. The motivation of finishing with six wins from six come the end of this international break should keep their standards high and prevent any drop in performance levels, so back the visitors to pick up another three points.
 Slovenia vs Switzerland tip: Switzerland to win
